stage_2_story.text_en:
Last Tuesday evening, Moshe sat in his favourite armchair with his grandson Yonatan, who is eleven years old and already knows everything about basketball. They were watching Maccabi Tel Aviv play against Hapoel Jerusalem — one of the biggest rivalries in Israeli basketball.

The game started at a fast pace. Maccabi's guard dribbled the length of the court and found the centre with a sharp assist. The centre caught the ball near the basket and finished with a strong dunk. The crowd in Menora Mivtachim Arena roared.

Moshe did not understand everything, so Yonatan explained patiently. 'Saba, when the guard brings the ball up and passes to a teammate who scores, that is called an assist,' Yonatan said.

In the second quarter, Maccabi's best player was fouled and walked to the foul line. He hit both free throws to stretch the lead. A moment later, Hapoel committed a turnover with a bad pass, and Maccabi scored immediately.

But Hapoel fought back. Their shooter stepped beyond the arc and hit a three-pointer to bring the crowd back into it. Then their tall centre won a rebound off a missed shot and scored.

By the end of the game, Moshe was leaning forward in his chair and shouting along with Yonatan. Maccabi won by four points. Walking to the kitchen to make tea, Moshe smiled and said: 'Yonatan, next time I want to go to the arena with you.'
